<!-- clinicos-review-handoff:v1 -->
{
  "kind": "report",
  "actor": "l2v-hub",
  "pr": 498,
  "subject_sha": "73775bbf7ddb2eabc61e2f1ea78b21895ab4c4a4",
  "request_id": "77bbb55c-f5e4-49b1-a1e9-6eca91689c38",
  "claim_id": "22ab3a4f-8ee5-4efc-9239-a172fa8d5be5",
  "round": 3,
  "report": {
    "subject_sha": "73775bbf7ddb2eabc61e2f1ea78b21895ab4c4a4",
    "verdict": "changes-requested",
    "summary": "Reviewed the delta 23eacd2a5..73775bbf7 (14 non-artifact files) with git reads only on the blobless clone. I ran no tests or code. Product commit f9eae82 named by packet 12 has an empty non-artifact diff against 73775bbf7, so the binding holds. CI on 73775bbf7: archive-tests, browser-e2e, bug-pipeline-tests, frontend-tests, gate, real-provider, secret-scan and windows-review-setup pass. Vercel fails on a rate limit, which is tolerated. Packet 12 (QA12: 1170 tests, 1167 pass, 3 skipped, plus 40 adversarial cases) is synthetic only. No real exact dispatch, recovery, preflight or production/demo deploy has been run, and I note that as an evidence limit. PREVIOUS FINDINGS. (1) MEDIUM exact-demo-dispatch.mjs:114, saved progress never recoverable: PARTIALLY RESOLVED. Failures in ensureExact, the prerequisites check, recordDeployment and publication now call persistExactBlock (release.mjs:417). It writes a durable releaseBlock {uuid, fixed code} plus releaseHold='exact-release-block', and hasReleaseHold/selectAutoReleaseBatch/assertNoReleaseHold honor it, so a plain retry cannot proceed or redispatch. It also posts a fixed sanitized marker comment and sets status 'Bloccato' on the PR and every issue, with no secrets or stderr. recoverExactRelease (release.mjs:~446) requires a manual workflow_dispatch with release_action=recover and the exact block UUID. authorizeReleaseRecovery (github.mjs) pins repo, ref main, the codex-bug-release workflow_ref@main, workflowSha==sha, actor==triggeringActor=='l2v-hub' and admin permission. It re-runs verifyCurrentCandidate (reviews, required checks, evidence) and checks that the original merge identity is unchanged. Post-merge it verifies by compare that the original merge is an ancestor of current main, with both endpoints re-read. verifyRetiredExactDispatches refuses any old run that is still active. Everything is re-checked inside the store-save guard. archiveRecovery keeps the old dispatches, block and release in exactReleaseRecoveries, and excludes old run IDs and dispatch IDs from the fresh intent. Post-merge recovery forces a fresh preflight against the new deploymentSha. Demo double deploy is avoided by the exact deploy's idle and identical-commit reuse, and the pipeline never dispatches production. Remaining gap: a saved intent with no observed run (POST failed, uncertain acknowledgement, or a guard/main change between saving intent and POSTing) can never be recovered (new finding 2). (2) MEDIUM release.mjs:353, production proof dropped: RESOLVED as to the gate, with a timing defect. assertDeploymentPrerequisites again requires RAILWAY_TOKEN for any backend change (release.mjs:367). recordDeployment and publishDeploymentCompletion require verifyProductionBackend (demo-deployment.mjs:948). That check binds the newest deploy-backend.yml run for the exact deploymentSha to repo, path, main, push/workflow_dispatch, attempt 1, completed and success, plus a single 'deploy' job whose 'Deploy to Railway' step succeeded. It re-reads the proof, hashes it, re-checks it at publication and persists it (publicationComplete requires it). The completion comment now links production and demo separately. However, nothing waits for the production run, so a deploy that is still running is treated as a failure and blocks durably (new finding 1). (3) LOW deploy-backend.yml:74, stale demo job: RESOLVED. The diff only removes lines 74-116 (demo job), with 0 added lines. The production 'deploy' job, its triggers, paths, concurrency group railway-backend and secrets are byte-identical. demo-workflow-policy.test.mjs asserts that deploy-backend has only the 'deploy' job and no RAILWAY_DEMO_TOKEN or demo-deployment.mjs, and that the exact workflow is the only demo deployer with preflight-exact before a single deploy-exact. Nothing else references the removed job. A vestigial 'operation' input remains (new finding 3). OTHER DELTA CHECKS. The release/confirm jobs now check out ${{ github.sha }} instead of refs/heads/main. That is an equal-or-stronger pin, since the jobs already require ref main. Concurrency groups are unchanged (codex-bug-pipeline, railway-demo, railway-backend). New steps add no new third-party actions, and persist-credentials stays false. Recovery inputs are restricted: release_action is a choice, mode is limited to release/record/recover in main(), and recovery requires event workflow_dispatch. Merge gates are unchanged: verifyCurrentCandidate, squash with match-head-commit, no admin. The demo deploy for a recovered deploymentSha re-checks ancestry and current main. Other changes are formatting only. Not verified: that CLINICOS_BOT_TOKEN authenticates as l2v-hub, which authorizeReleaseRecovery requires; otherwise recovery is impossible by design.",
    "findings": [
      {
        "severity": "medium",
        "file": "agent-team/src/bug-pipeline/release.mjs",
        "line": 905,
        "problem": "recordDeployment calls verifyProductionBackend once, with no wait. codex-bug-release.yml no longer waits for the push-triggered deploy-backend.yml run (the comment at the runtime step says missing proof 'blocks'). confirm-demo runs right after the release job. The production run for the merge SHA (railway up --ci, a build plus prisma migrate deploy) can still be queued or in_progress at that point, because it runs in parallel with the demo deploy. It may also be serialized behind an earlier backend deploy in concurrency group railway-backend. verifyProductionBackend (demo-deployment.mjs:1001) treats any non-completed status as PRODUCTION_PROOF_FAILED, and a run not yet created as PRODUCTION_RUN_REQUIRED. The catch at release.mjs:933 then calls persistExactBlock, which durably blocks the batch, marks the PR and issues 'Bloccato' and requires an owner recovery. That recovery re-preflights and re-dispatches demo even though nothing failed. A normal, healthy release can therefore end blocked depending only on timing. A related problem: after a post-merge recovery, deploymentSha is the current main. If that head commit did not touch the deploy-backend.yml path filters, no production run will ever exist for it. The block text gives no hint that a manual deploy-backend operation=deploy is needed, so recover, record and block can repeat.",
        "requested_change": "Before evaluating production proof in record mode, add a bounded read-only wait for the deploy-backend.yml run for deploymentSha to appear and complete (for example up to 60 min, polling the same fixed inventory, never dispatching). Wait while the run is missing, queued, in_progress, waiting or pending. Only a completed non-success run, attempt>1, an identity mismatch or a timeout should become a durable block. Use a distinct code for timeout or missing run (for example PRODUCTION_RUN_PENDING_TIMEOUT) versus PRODUCTION_PROOF_FAILED. Alternatively, restore an equivalent wait step in codex-bug-release.yml before confirm-demo. When the block code is PRODUCTION_RUN_REQUIRED, make the fixed block text say that a production deploy of that exact SHA must exist (for example a manual deploy-backend dispatch on main), without implying that the pipeline will dispatch it.",
        "test_expectation": "A release.test (or demo-deployment.test) where the production run for deploymentSha is first absent, then in_progress, then completed/success. The wait polls and records 'deployed' with no releaseBlock, no 'Bloccato' status and no dispatch. The same sequence ending in completed/failure, or a timeout, yields exactly one durable block with the right code and the issues still open. A test where in_progress never completes within the bound yields the timeout code, not PRODUCTION_PROOF_FAILED."
      },
      {
        "severity": "medium",
        "file": "agent-team/src/bug-pipeline/exact-demo-dispatch.mjs",
        "line": 236,
        "problem": "verifyRetiredExactDispatches requires exactly one correlated run for any saved progress without runId. Otherwise it fails with 'uncertain old dispatch cannot be recovered'. ensure() saves phase 'intent' durably (line 153) before guard(), currentMain(sha) and the POST (lines 154-159). It saves 'submitted' after an acknowledgement that may be uncertain (createExactDispatchPoster line 53-54: 'dispatch acknowledgement uncertain; intent retained'). So if the POST is rejected or fails (for example a 4xx/5xx or timeout), or if main moves or the guard fails between line 153 and the POST, the batch is durably blocked (EXACT_MAIN_CHANGED / EXACT_DISPATCH_BLOCKED). No correlated run will ever exist, and recoverExactRelease can never succeed. The only way out is hand-editing durable state, which is the condition finding 1 of the previous round asked to remove. The progress record has no timestamp, so a settle window cannot be applied either.",
        "requested_change": "Record an intent timestamp (and a submitted timestamp) in the saved progress. In verifyRetiredExactDispatches, allow retiring a progress that has no runId only when: (a) at least a fixed settle window (for example 15 min, longer than GitHub's dispatch-to-run latency) has passed since intent; (b) two complete, bounded inventory reads separated in time for that SHA show zero runs with that dispatch's exact display_title; (c) its dispatchId is then added to excludedDispatchIds. Also make the fresh ensure() fail closed (no POST) if any run titled with an excluded dispatchId later appears in the inventory for the SHA. Keep the current refusal inside the settle window and for ambiguous (more than one) matches.",
        "test_expectation": "Tests in exact-demo-dispatch.test/release.test where: (1) postDispatch rejects after intent is saved; (2) main changes between saving intent and the POST; (3) the acknowledgement is uncertain and no run ever appears. Each yields a durable block. Recovery inside the settle window is rejected. Recovery after the window with two empty inventory reads archives the progress, excludes its dispatchId and allows exactly one new POST. A late-appearing run with the old title causes the new ensure() to fail closed with no POST."
      },
      {
        "severity": "low",
        "file": ".github/workflows/deploy-backend.yml",
        "line": 31,
        "problem": "The workflow_dispatch input 'operation' (options preflight/deploy, default preflight) is now vestigial, because the preflight-only demo job was removed. A manual dispatch with the default value creates a run on the current main SHA whose only job, 'deploy', is skipped, and the run may conclude success. verifyProductionBackend (agent-team/src/bug-pipeline/demo-deployment.mjs:979) selects the newest run by id for the SHA. That skipped-deploy run shadows the real successful push deploy and makes record/publication fail with PRODUCTION_PROOF_FAILED, leading to a durable block. This is also exactly what an operator might do when following up on finding 1 above.",
        "requested_change": "Remove the 'operation' input, so that workflow_dispatch always means deploy of that exact main commit and the job if-condition is just the main ref. Alternatively, have verifyProductionBackend ignore runs whose 'deploy' job is skipped when selecting the newest candidate, while still failing on any newer failed or in-progress deploy run. Update the input description and demo-workflow-policy.test.mjs accordingly.",
        "test_expectation": "demo-workflow-policy.test.mjs asserts that deploy-backend.yml has no 'preflight' operation input, or no input at all. A demo-deployment.test where the newest run for the SHA is a workflow_dispatch run with the deploy job skipped either cannot occur structurally or is ignored, while a newer failed or in-progress deploy run still blocks."
      }
    ]
  }
}
